name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes where other upscalers blur edges or lose depth cues—critical for excavator footage where terrain edges and small objects matter. The trade-off is higher VRAM usage and slower processing, but the 0.5%+ quality gain justifies it for high-stakes inspections.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is motion blur in fast excavator footage, not depth loss—adding depth upscaling just masks the wrong symptom. Instead, test RealVisXL’s face-preserving upscaler first; if face fidelity improves even 0.5%, that’s the real gain. Settle it with a blind A/B test: run both upscalers on identical footage, measure face clarity and terrain edge retention, and compare the numbers.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL 5.0’s face-preserving upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline now. Faces in excavator footage are often the clearest human signal—operators, inspectors, safety teams—and losing fidelity here breaks downstream tasks like compliance checks or training models. The trade-off is higher compute cost per frame, but we gain a measurable boost in usable data where it matters most.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s core flaw—it’s a bandage on motion blur, not the root cause. The real risk is wasting compute on a symptom while the footage’s fast motion still degrades all frames. Test a motion-deblurring model first; if face fidelity improves after that, then upscaling adds value—otherwise, it’s just expensive noise reduction.
